name: שְׁדֵיאוּר
gloss: Shaddai is light; or light of Shaddai
summary: A man of Reuben in the wilderness, known only as the father of Elizur, the prince of Reuben at the numbering and in the march (Num 1:5; 10:18). The name joins שַׁדַּי, the name God gave himself to the fathers (Gen 17:1; Exo 6:3), to אוּר, “light, flame”, as אוּרִיאֵל and אוּרִיָּה join light to אֵל and יָהּ, and as Psa 27:1 says “Yahweh is my light”. The first part is not spelled in full (שְׁדֵי־ for שַׁדַּי), so the reading rests on its form and on the other Shaddai names of the same lists, Zurishaddai and Ammishaddai.

evidence.note: The standard of the camp of Reuben set out, “and over its host Elizur son of שְׁדֵיאוּר”.
Elizur son of Shedeur brings Reuben’s offering on the fourth day (and 7:35).
The next name in the list: Shelumiel son of צוּרִישַׁדָּי, “my rock is Shaddai”.
Ahiezer son of עַמִּישַׁדָּי: Shaddai names in the same list.
“I am אֵל שַׁדַּי; walk before me and be whole.”
“Yahweh is my אוֹר and my salvation”: the sentence such names make.
Punic personal name ʾRBʿL “Baal is his light”: a god’s name joined to ʾr “light”, the same pattern.

note: BDB files the name under שדה (v.bh.ad, n.pr.m. in Reuben, no gloss); the name’s second element is this root’s אוּר/אוֹר, so it is linked to the entry or. Whether the first element is שַׁדַּי or another word (שַׁד, breast, or שָׂדֶה, field) is not settled by any verse; “Shaddai is light” is taken as the reading the other names of Num 1:5–15 favour. The name occurs at Num 1:5; 2:10; 7:30, 35; 10:18.
